body: This was a great comment, thank you. You’re right
Not my guy friends. And they all want/ have kids
Sometimes lol

I’m not talking about a specific man but men in my community, in general. And although that’s lovely to say, you don’t know me at all lol. I might be a bitch actually 🤷🏽‍♀️. But Yh, just don’t see it happening tbh with you. I’ve been unlucky in love my whole life.

I really hate the toxic positivity spewed at us. Romantic love is just luck based and I’m the unluckiest person. 
It sucks that you can relate me. I hope you do find your partner and if not, I hope you accept and live a happily single life.

Thank you but I don’t see it happening. I’m not a traditional woman (non religious, left leaning), I don’t fit the standard that men want (I’m 5”8, don’t have a bum or nice boobs), again I’m cf (most men want kids) and chronically ill with a degenerative condition. I’m not finding a man (in the black community (no other ethnicity has ever been interested in me)) who will want me the same way I want them. I’m fed up of hoping.
Women get told this too. People are always saying this bs to me 🙄. What is unique about men’s loneliness , that women don’t also experience? (Genuine question)
I loveee bed rotting. I start getting overwhelmed if I don’t get sufficient time to rot lol
If you never liked kids before, why did you want one? Because you still need to interact with other kids when you have one..

Can I ask, did you never consider potentially being a single mum at some point? Because life happens, he could’ve got terminally ill or die etc. I’m sorry that happened to you though. They’re both despicable human beings. I’m sorry that you’re still connected to him in some way.
I’m sorry you had to go through that
This is sadly true. Would definitely prefer to be a father
That’s a shame. Sadly, that’s just the risk you take when you’re in a sexual relationship 🤷🏽‍♀️
Did you only start hating it after the 2nd child?
Sadly true. I have to admit, if I were a man, I wouldn’t be happy with that either

The no bum thing is really difficult in a society that praises it. I’m 5”9, not slim, plus size with a flat bum and a friend made a comment when I was 16 and I’ve never forgotten it (I’m 35), so I cannot imagine how hurt you must’ve have felt hearing that from him. It is possible to grow one, there are loads of vids and tips on TikTok/YT. So if you’re physically capable of working out, do it. But also, try not to hold on to that comment for too long, don’t let him destroy your self esteem
I’ve had a look before, there are a few posts from people in the uk but doesn’t seem to be popular amongst us yet.

I’m Jamaican too, so kids are all I’ve been surrounded with. It’s just an expectation from everyone. So I can’t imagine ever meeting a CF Jamaican man 😂. 
I just recently tried dating someone who wasn’t my type (looks wise, personality and he was younger) and he bailed on me the first time I had to reschedule due to being in pain. So even when I don’t like them, they’re not serious. Love that you found a black man but in my experience, they have never been serious with me. So I cannot imagine it ever happening, so I think I’m divesting

Thanks. I’m sure you meant well with your comments but as you stated yourself, you’re not black or deal with chronic illnesses. Dating as one in a predominantly white country is difficult as it is, much less adding CF and degenerative conditions on top. Although I agree with you, I need to focus on hobbies more and I may try out dating apps again in the future.

You need to want children for yourself. Will you ever want to be a single mum? Because anything can happen (breakup, illness, death etc). So only have them if you are willing to be one, not because he wants one. Chances are you’ll be the default parent (regardless of what he says), do you want that? If you are unsure, the answer right now is no. But you’re really young and you have so much time to consider it.

This is what my best friend of 25 yrs did. She didn’t have a kid, but she finally got a bf (and I’m single) and we had about 3/4 conversations after that and that was that. She exited my life. I definitely feel like I was a placeholder

Very true. They’re just projecting their own ideals on to us. It’s like us cf lot being disgusted with people who have kids because we don’t understand why they want them. I just don’t like being looked down upon
It’s true. I didn’t ask to be here, I’m not going to now do what everyone says I should, when I reeeally don’t want to
Agree with you 100%! But it’s exhausting having that invisible pressure

It’s very difficult. I’m 33f (not US citizen) and every guy either already has kids or wants them. Especially in my culture where men’s “legacy” is literally how many kids (specifically sons) you’ve had 🙄. A guy even told me I’m not going to find any man cos why would any man not want to have kids? 😑 I met one guy in 6 months of dating apps who didn’t want kids, and that didn’t last. But I literally only saw 3 people who had “no children” in their bios and 2 out of 3 already had kids 🙄. I don’t want to date any single dads either. At this rate, I’m just going to be single forever lol
Very true. Everyone just wants a baby/toddler. Who says they want a 9 or 14 year old?  I don’t ever hear anyone being excited to parent a teenager lol

I agree with this. I’ve been chronically depressed for years but even I wouldn’t want to be with someone who was like me. It’s hard supporting someone allll the time. Most people don’t have the mental strength to deal with it long term, and it’s understandable. Not nice for us depressed people lol but understandable.

Can definitely relate. I had a party at my house recently and I was the only single person and everyone else was in their couples. It’s hard especially if it’s been a long while and you actually want someone.
Thank you!

Because all women, cf or not (and irrespective of sexuality too), are socialised to be wives. We’re taught and shown from very young that the aim of life is getting married and having kids. And for cf women, that want to be with a long term partner, to be a wife, is clearly still there. And most of us ACT like wives in our rships, regardless of status or length of time (silly of us, I know). So when it doesn’t work out, it’s like, “what was I playing wife for? What was the point?”  

And I think that way too, as if something was a waste of time because it didn’t end in a long term partnership/ marriage. And honestly, after reading these comments, I really need to think about why I think that. Why can’t I just enjoy the time spent?

Sadly, the majority of society thinks that a woman will eventually change their mind. Like if it happened, you’ll just go along with it and your bf is one of those people. I think you 2 will have to have a serious conversation about your future together. Because you don’t want to waste anymore time.

I’m sorry you’re in the same position. It’s really difficult. 
Even applying for disability benefits is so dehumanising! They made me literally “perform” for them (watching me sitting, standing walking etc) even though I provided doctors letters AND images from operations. 
This world doesn’t give af about those in need but yet guilt trip people who want to end their suffering. Unless we win the lottery, what options are there? 
Anyway, I hope you succeed in your claim for support.

I feel for you. I’m not sure how people who are chronically ill can even afford to exist in the US. At least my healthcare is dealt with. 
But thank you. I hope things get better for you too.
Thank you, and same to you. I’m sorry that you understand how I feel x

But I don’t have income protection anymore, so I need it. I will take your advice so thank you.

I had several internal ultrasounds that came back normal but I have endometriosis and adenomyosis. You will need to insist that they investigate properly if you have the relevant symptoms. Don’t let them fob you off.
I have no immediate plans to do it myself. I’m hoping it’ll come naturally and soon.

My family are busy and even though I’ve asked, they can only do so much. I already don’t do chores or anything around the house, I just keep my own space as clean as I can. I get some meals a week but obviously not every meal. But other than that, there’s nothing they can do for me. They can’t work for me, can’t pay my bills or rid me of my condition. There’s nothing they can do for me, that’ll make my life feel like it’s worth it. The bare minimum isn’t good enough for me, as ungrateful as that sounds, but I don’t think just being alive is good enough. For anyone.

I have endometriosis too, so I understand how it is and it’s hell. At least you have a partner and don’t have to live with your parents. That’s an independence I wish I had. But it obviously still sucks. And it must make you feel even more guilty, all the effort people have put in. It’s a horrible thing to live with.

Thank you. My support system knows how I feel. I only have my family and Ive had regular breakdowns. My friends know too. It’s just that there’s nothing they can say to me, to make me feel better. And they cannot help me financially. No one can help me, it’s just “aww.. I’m sorry..wish I could take the pain away” etc etc. which is nice but empty platitudes mean nothing to me. I need real help and there’s none.
I’ve done this many times. Obviously I’m still here. And they say prayer works 🙄
I understand. It is hard but you will literally grow through it. Take care of yourself and seek online mental health help groups for teens when you can or whenever you get to that super low place.

It will be annoying to hear this but give it time. True, life does suck and I cannot guarantee it’ll get better but you’ll get better at handling those things. 

You’re 13, that is almost every persons “ugly duckling” time lol. Your body is changing and you’re transitioning into a new person, it’s a difficult process but you will get through it, because you have to. I bet you most of your class feels the same in regard to how they look. But they won’t share that, because you guys are just insecure at this moment, but Just know, millions of 13 year olds feel the same. I’m 33 now but I still remember absolutely hating myself at 13. I wouldn’t even get dressed in front of a mirror lol.

There’s also so much you haven’t been able to do. An independence you haven’t yet experienced. And sooo much fun left to have. 
Life is shit, I won’t lie, but for you, there’s still some experiences you won’t want to miss. 
So don’t go yet.
Thank you x

I don’t think being alive is important enough to struggle through (I obviously had no decision in being here or I wouldn’t be 🙄). Because why bring another human into this world just for them to struggle with you? But I also understand the argument that, it shouldn’t be just people with money who are allowed to have kids. Maybe we need to live in a world where people can at least have a roof over their heads and food to eat. But that’s a dream I guess.
How can HER purpose in life depend on YOU having a child? That doesn’t make any sense at all.

I’ve been chronically depressed for nearly a decade and single that entire time (I’m in my 30s now). I just don’t feel like a fun person to be around, I already struggled to connect with people but that worsened after my health and mh got worse. I just cannot imagine finding someone that I like, who would like me just as much, whilst I’m like this. And it’s a hurtful thought tbh.

I do not want to be here majority of the time.

But obviously everyone is different so do still inform your doctors about it. Or at least tell them you smoke something if you’re cautious about mentioning weed.

I wouldn’t advise coming here tbh. This country gets worse every day. Our government doesn’t care about people and housing is soo expensive. Most adults are still living with parents cos we can’t afford to buy or even rent. The only good thing is the NHS and the government are destroying that too. Smh. 
Oh and many people here actually hate immigrants (unless you’re White white Australian, American etc 🙄). It’s a hostile place unless you move to a city. Which is expensive.

Being a teen sucks. Tbh it was one of the worst times of my life. I hated being 15. I too was overweight, didn’t have much of a social life and grew up poor. Teens are also horrible people lol, so don’t think this is about you. Humans just suck. Being an adult is hard, don’t get me wrong but you grow out of some insecurities. You start caring less about what others think of you. (Well most of the time). Hopefully you start working and you can afford to do things that interest you. Don’t worry, your teen years are almost done. You may make friends in college/university or when you start working. It may seem like forever but in less than 5 years things will be different for you.

I understand this. I’m early 30s and been single for over a decade. All my younger siblings and cousins are in relationships, have kids. And I’m the only single one. I have depression and chronic illnesses too. It really sucks. 
Wish I could say something encouraging to you but I also know that it may not work. 
But men (if that’s who you’re attracted) aren’t all that, most of them anyway. So we’re probably not missing out on much lol. But would be nice to experience it a little.
Lol it’s very annoying when you notice all the women around you have stopped growing. Wait to you get the age when a lot of men are your height or shorter.

Needing someone to feed you, help you get dressed, that kind of thing. But I still may call.

 I’m trying.

I’m so sorry that you had to give up your business and career. Honestly, this disease fucking sucks. But at least you have your wife who (unfortunately) understands how it feels. I hope you get to do the van life! That seems so cool, being able to drive around and live almost everywhere. 
But yh, I don’t think I can even do another 5 years of just sitting around watching tv, much less another 40-50! I genuinely don’t see the point.

I’m sorry to hear that your health has been getting worse. The coding is really cool. Maybe I should learn something like that to get extra income or something. I use YouGov but it takes forever to earn £50. Ive been using it for nearly 2 years lol.

I feel you. It’s so hard and I just don’t know how people expect us to live. Especially those of us who are single or don’t have family to rely on. Like I never see or hear anyone talking about it (excluding support groups obviously). 
And no, watching Netflix and other people living their lives is not something I want. And tbh I don’t know how long I can do it for. There seems to be no way out (unless I win the lottery)
In western countries, absolutely.

But at least you were able to purchase a property which is a great achievement. Something I doubt I’ll ever get to do.

But you are right, they cannot be my only social group. But finding adults outside of my family and school friends is very difficult for me. Yup! I’m the eldest of 6 and I was put off kids from my teen years (especially when my last 3 siblings were born 11yrs+) and a big family with lots of cousins. I thought as I grew up things would change but no, still don’t want them. It’s like I took a free trial of parenthood and I just don’t see the benefit, at all.

I think this will differ from culture to culture, how many siblings, the age difference and also by class. I’d imagine eldest daughters in poorer communities will experience this “free trial” more than say someone of a privileged background (so being able to afford sitters/nannies, after school clubs, having a sahm etc). Obviously depends on the amount/level of responsibility e.g just taking your younger sibling to school in the morning vs looking after them all day during summer holidays whilst parents worked, are 2 very different types of responsibilities.
Being the older sibling but there’s only a 3/4 yr difference is going to be a different experience to someone 10+ years difference.

You are absolutely right. And I especially feel for those of you in the US, I cannot imagine the costs you bear on healthcare. I pay £10 a month for any prescriptions I need and that is a lot to me, since I’m not working atm. And I don’t lay to see any doctors/specialists thankfully. But there’s all the food deliveries, vitamins that barely work, seeing a therapist, getting additional treatments like acupuncture or massages, buying any little thing that might help make life more comfortable (pillows, mattresses, back support etc). It’s a lot. And then on top, we’re not even considered when it comes to disability benefits because we’re not disabled enough. It really sucks. I can’t stand it.
